title: Point transport on whole coefficient systems, powers and integral realization
statement:
Fix $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, its algebraic closure $k$, $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, $R=\mathcal O_E$, a uniformizer $\varpi$, and $A_n=R/\varpi^n$, as in [def-trf-coefficient-conventions]. Put $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$ and $h=\operatorname{Spec}(\gamma)$ for geometric Frobenius [def-trf-scheme-frobenius]. On the small pro-etale site of $s$, set $B_n=(A_n)_s$ and $\widehat R_s=\lim_n B_n$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Use the abelian category $\mathscr S_s$ of strict semilinear $B_n$-module systems and its unbounded derived category [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]. Write $U_s$ for levelwise restriction to $\widehat R_s$-module towers, $\mathcal L_s=R\lim U_s$, and $\mathcal R_sN$ for the simultaneous derived reduction system [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus]. Let $G_r$ be exact termwise inverse image along $h^r$, using the canonical coefficient isomorphisms. Its levels are identified with the termwise module pullbacks $(h^r)^*M_n=(h^r)^{-1}M_n\otimes_{(h^r)^{-1}B_n}B_n$ by the isomorphisms $j_r:x\mapsto x\otimes1$ of [def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison], part (a); every map below is read through this identification, so that the finite point transports land in $\Gamma(s,L(h^r)^*C_n)$. Let $t_m:G_1G_m\xrightarrow{\sim}G_{m+1}$ be the canonical inverse-image compositor, in the direction inverse to [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition]. Define $\Gamma_\bullet C$ by applying restriction of scalars and $\Gamma(s,-)$ to each level of a complex of systems; it is a functor $D(\mathscr S_s)\to D(\operatorname{Tow}(\operatorname{Mod}R))$ [lem-weil-point-proetale-sections-exact].

For EVERY $C\in D(\mathscr S_s)$, not necessarily a reduction system of an integral input, restriction along $h^r$, insertion into the inverse-image colimit and sheafification, and $x\mapsto x\otimes1$ at each level, in the recipe of [def-weil-frobenius-point-transport], define a specified natural tower map
$$I_{r,C}:\Gamma_\bullet C\longrightarrow\Gamma_\bullet G_rC.$$
The recipe is applied to complexes of whole semilinear systems before localization; its transition maps are the given semilinear transitions of $C$. If the evaluations $C_n$ are bounded constructible, the evaluation of $I_{r,C}$ is exactly the finite point transport $\iota^{(r)}_{C_n}$. For every derived SYSTEM morphism $u:C\to D$, and every $m\geq1$, the following are identities in the derived category of whole $R$-module towers:
$$\Gamma_\bullet(G_ru)\circ I_{r,C}=I_{r,D}\circ\Gamma_\bullet(u),$$
$$I_{m+1,C}=\Gamma_\bullet(t_{m,C})\circ I_{1,G_mC}\circ I_{m,C}.$$

Here is the realization normalization, including its actual comparison maps. Put $N=\mathcal L_sC$ and assume only $N\in D^b_c(s,R)$ [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed]. Write $P_r=L(h^r)^*$ for completed integral pullback [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. Let
$$\nu_{r,C}:P_rN\xrightarrow{\sim}(h^r)^{-1}N\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal L_sG_rC$$
use the coefficient isomorphism $ (h^r)^{-1}\widehat R_s\cong\widehat R_s$, the INVERSE of the specified integral map $\kappa_N:(h^r)^{-1}N\to P_rN$ of [def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison], part (b), and commutation of the exact inverse-image equivalence with the total derived limit [lem-weil-proetale-isomorphism-inverse-image]. The assertion includes invertibility of this specified $\kappa_N$ on the stated derived-complete domain. The latter comparison is the derived map of the entire limit cone: on a tower resolution it is inverse image applied to its limit-cone map, not a choice of identifications of individual evaluations. Let $\zeta_C:R\lim\Gamma_\bullet C\xrightarrow{\sim}\Gamma(s,\mathcal L_sC)$ be the comparison induced by applying exact sections, which preserve products, to the total-limit model [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit]. Then the actual maps satisfy
$$\zeta_{G_rC}\circ R\lim(I_{r,C})=\Gamma(s,\nu_{r,C})\circ\iota_N^{(r)}\circ\zeta_C.$$
All these comparisons are natural for system morphisms. They respect the compositors as follows. The object $P_mN$ lies in $D^b_c(s,R)$ [lem-weil-isomorphism-derived-pullback], hence so does $\mathcal L_sG_mC\cong P_mN$, and $\nu_{1,G_mC}$ is defined. Let $c^E_{m,N}:P_{m+1}N\xrightarrow{\sim}P_1P_mN$ be the specified integral pullback-composition isomorphism of [lem-trf-integral-pullback-comparison-realization] for $h$ followed by $h^m$. Then
$$\nu_{m+1,C}=\mathcal L_s(t_{m,C})\circ\nu_{1,G_mC}\circ P_1(\nu_{m,C})\circ c^E_{m,N}.$$
 In particular for $C=\mathcal R_sN$ this recovers the powerwise version of [lem-trf-integral-point-transport-tower-realization]; the formula also applies directly to a finite-output compact-support system with bounded constructible derived limit. No finite Tor-amplitude, normalization, or reconstruction assumption on $C$ is imposed.

source.place: Agent-formulated prerequisite to clause (3): point transport on arbitrary simultaneous output systems and its whole-limit normalization; the blueprint asserts the application, not this stronger comparison lemma.

proof.text: Put $F_r=(h^r)^{-1}$, with the module action transported through the specified coefficient isomorphism. The site-equivalence description in [lem-weil-proetale-isomorphism-inverse-image](1) identifies $(F_rM)(U\to s)$ with $M(U\xrightarrow{h^r\circ u}s)$. Under it the restriction/colimit-insertion/sheafification map $\sigma_{r,M}$ in [def-weil-frobenius-point-transport] is exactly restriction along $h^r$ at the final object. Indeed its colimit index is $(s\xrightarrow{h^r}s)$ and its coprojection is the reindexing identification at that object. The coefficient isomorphism sends the insertion of a constant $a\in A_n$ to the same constant $a$, by its definition in [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. Thus $\sigma_{r,M}$ is $A_n$-linear. The finite tensor comparison $j_{r,M}:F_rM\to(h^r)^*M$, $x\mapsto x\otimes1$, has inverse $x\otimes a\mapsto c_n^{-1}(a)x$, by balancing. These formulas hold for every module, without constructibility. They identify the tensor-pullback model of $G_r$ with $F_r$; below we retain $j_r$ whenever the tensor model is used.

source.place: Clause (3): identify the explicit point-transport recipe with restriction in the automorphism reindexing model

proof.text: Represent $C$ by a complex of strict semilinear systems $M$. At level $n$ define $u_{r,n}=\Gamma(j_{r,M_n})\sigma_{r,M_n}$. A differential or a transition $v:M_{n+1}\to\operatorname{Res}M_n$ is a map of underlying sheaves. Its restrictions commute with $\operatorname{res}_{h^r}$, and its inverse image commutes with the colimit coprojections and sheafification maps. At the tensor insertion, applying the coefficient quotient $\rho_n:B_{n+1}\to B_n$ sends $x\otimes1$ to $v(x)\otimes\rho_n(1)=v(x)\otimes1$. The coefficient square $\pi_nc_{\widehat R}=c_nF_r(\pi_n)$ in [def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison] makes this equation $\widehat R_s$-linear after restriction. Hence $u_{r,\bullet}$ is a chain map of whole $R$-module towers, with the original transitions of $M$. A chain map $f:M\to M'$ satisfies $\Gamma_\bullet(G_rf)u_{r,M}=u_{r,M'}\Gamma_\bullet(f)$ by the same restriction and tensor formulas. Its level $n$ is the stated finite point transport whenever that derived evaluation is bounded constructible, since this is its defining recipe.

source.place: Clause (3): form the map on strict whole systems, including arbitrary semilinear transitions

proof.text: Restriction of scalars is exact: it changes only the scalar action, leaving kernels and cokernels of underlying abelian sheaves unchanged. Exactness of systems is componentwise, as in [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus]. The functor $G_r$ is exact by the equivalence of [lem-weil-proetale-isomorphism-inverse-image], and sections are exact by [lem-weil-point-proetale-sections-exact]. Consequently the two functors between complex categories used in step 2 preserve quasi-isomorphisms. Their natural chain transformation therefore localizes to a specified $I_r$ on $D(\mathscr S_s)$. Explicitly, the commutative square of step 2 for each arrow of a roof $C\xleftarrow{a}M\xrightarrow{b}D$, with $a$ a quasi-isomorphism of systems, also commutes after inverting the images of $a$. This proves the asserted naturality for every derived SYSTEM morphism, without trying to lift an arbitrary family of evaluated maps.

source.place: Clause (3): localize the whole-system natural transformation

proof.text: Check the power formula before localization in the reindexing model of step 1. The two successive restrictions, first along $h^m$ and then along $h$, are restriction along $h^m\circ h=h^{m+1}$ by the sheaf restriction axiom. The inverse-image compositor identifies $F_1F_mM$ with $F_{m+1}M$ by associating these same site reindexings. In the tensor model its inverse is the termwise canonical module-pullback comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition]; multiplying the two inserted units sends $(x\otimes1)\otimes1$ to $x\otimes1$. Thus it is precisely the specified $t_m$, and on the whole strict tower $u_{m+1,M}=\Gamma_\bullet(t_{m,M})u_{1,G_mM}u_{m,M}$. This is an equality of chain maps: the restriction calculation is in every degree and commutes with the actual transitions checked in step 2. Localization gives the displayed power identity in the derived tower category.

source.place: Ancestor thm-trf-l-function-euler-product, Step 1, Global powers: composition of the point-transport factors

proof.text: For a strict tower complex $X$, use $H(X)=\operatorname{Cone}(1-s_X)[-1]$ in the coordinates $H(X)^i=(\prod_nX_n^{i-1})\oplus(\prod_nX_n^i)$, $d(b,a)=(-db-(1-s_X)a,da)$. Products of sheaf modules on $s_{\mathrm{proet}}$ are sectionwise and exact by [lem-weil-proetale-countable-products-exact]. Products of $R$-modules are exact too: choose a preimage in each coordinate of a family of surjections. Regard $R$-modules as modules on the one-object trivial site. Thus [lem-weil-strict-roos-comparison] identifies these cone functors, including their maps and strict augmentations, with TOTAL derived inverse limit. The completed-module functor $F_r$ is exact by [def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison] and preserves products by the site reindexing of step 1. Sections are exact by [lem-weil-point-proetale-sections-exact] and preserve products because they are sectionwise. Apply [lem-cbc-exact-product-functor-strict-limit] to these two functors. It gives the specified natural comparisons $a_{r,C}:F_r\mathcal L_sC\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal L_sG_rC$ (including $j_r$) and $\zeta_C:R\lim\Gamma_\bullet C\xrightarrow{\sim}\Gamma(s,\mathcal L_sC)$, the latter in the inverse direction to that lemma's comparison. In cone coordinates the comparisons are the canonical product comparisons on BOTH summands, with no extra off-diagonal term. The lemma's resolution normalization identifies them with applying inverse image, respectively sections, to the entire limit cone.

source.place: Clause (3): specified whole-limit comparisons, using Stacks Tag 0941 (lemma-derived-limit-is-ok) and its normalized strict Roos refinement

proof.text:
Write $X=U_sM$ and $N=H(X)$ for the moment. Under the comparisons of step 5, $R\lim(I_{r,C})$ is the actual two-component chain map $H(u_r)(b,a)=((\prod_nu_{r,n})b,(\prod_nu_{r,n})a)$. This is a chain map because the transition equation in step 2 gives $(1-s_{G_rX})\prod u_{r,n}=(\prod u_{r,n})(1-s_X)$. On a product sheaf, restriction sends $(x_n)_n$ to $(x_n|_{h^r})_n$. Hence $\sigma_{r,\prod X_n}$, followed by the canonical inverse-image product comparison, is $\prod_n\sigma_{r,X_n}$. Restriction also preserves the two direct-sum coordinates in $H(X)$. Consequently, on BOTH the shifted and unshifted coordinates, $H(u_r)$ equals sections of the cone comparison $a_{r,C}$ after $\sigma_{r,H(X)}$. The natural normalized cone identifications of [lem-weil-strict-roos-comparison] therefore give
$$\zeta_{G_rC}R\lim(I_{r,C})=\Gamma(s,a_{r,C})\sigma_{r,\mathcal L_sC}\zeta_C.$$
This calculation proves an equality of derived maps on whole systems; it does not infer it from equality after projection to each $n$.

source.place: Clause (3): compare point transport on both coordinates of the whole derived-limit cone

proof.text:
Now assume $N=\mathcal L_sC\in D^b_c(s,R)$. Choose a flat-term K-flat resolution $Q\to N$ by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution] and write $Q_n=Q\otimes_{\widehat R_s}B_n$. The $L=E$ case of [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison] gives the natural isomorphism $\chi_N:N\to H((\operatorname{Res}_nQ_n)_n)$, represented on $Q$ by $z\mapsto(0,(z\otimes1)_n)$. It applies because derived completeness is part of [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed]. Applying exact $F_r$, its product comparison and the tower isomorphisms $j_{r,Q_n}$ of step 1 gives an isomorphism
$$F_rN\xrightarrow{F_r\chi_N}F_rH(Q_\bullet)\xrightarrow{\sim}H(F_rQ_\bullet)\xrightarrow{H(j_r)}H(((h^r)^*Q_n)_n)=P_rN.$$
On $F_rQ$ its formula is $w\mapsto(0,(j_{r,Q_n}F_r(z\mapsto z\otimes1)(w))_n)$. This is EXACTLY the map $\tilde\theta$ defining part (b) of [def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison], followed by the inverse of $F_r(Q\to N)$. Thus the displayed isomorphism is the specified $\kappa_N$, not merely some isomorphism with the same reductions. Independence and naturality follow from the resolution-independent natural completion comparison, the product comparison in step 5, and the functorial descent in [lem-pur-integral-operations-well-defined].

source.place: Clause (3): identify and invert the actual integral comparison (b), via the natural completion augmentation of Bhatt-Scholze Definition 3.5.2

proof.text:
By definition the stated realization comparison is $
u_{r,C}=a_{r,C}\kappa_N^{-1}$. The integral transport of [def-weil-frobenius-point-transport], with the recipe applied to $h^r$, is $\iota_N^{(r)}=\Gamma(s,\kappa_N)\sigma_{r,N}$. Therefore $\Gamma(s,
u_{r,C})\iota_N^{(r)}=\Gamma(s,a_{r,C})\sigma_{r,N}$ by cancellation of the actual $\kappa_N$ and its inverse. Substitution into the equality of step 6 proves precisely
$$\zeta_{G_rC}R\lim(I_{r,C})=\Gamma(s,
u_{r,C})\iota_N^{(r)}\zeta_C.$$
The assumption is only on $N$; nowhere was $C$ replaced by the reduction system of $N$.

source.place: Clause (3): the normalization identity with the specified nu and iota, without reconstruction of C

proof.text:
Naturality: the product comparisons and normalized Roos identifications are natural on the derived tower category by [lem-cbc-exact-product-functor-strict-limit] and [lem-weil-strict-roos-comparison], and step 7 makes $\kappa_N$ natural and invertible on $D^b_c(s,R)$. Inverse-image side: put $d_m:F_1F_m\xrightarrow{\sim}F_{m+1}$ for site reindexing. On either cone summand
$$a_{m+1,C}d_{m,N}=\mathcal L_s(t_{m,C})a_{1,G_mC}F_1(a_{m,C}),$$
since projecting either product gives the same twice-reindexed projection with the same tensor units multiplied, as in step 4, and the universal property of the product identifies the summand maps. Pullback side: $P_mN\in D^b_c(s,R)$ by [lem-weil-isomorphism-derived-pullback], and [lem-trf-integral-inverse-image-comparison-composition] for $h$ followed by $h^m$ gives $c^E_{m,N}\kappa^{(m+1)}_Nd_{m,N}=\kappa^{(1)}_{P_mN}F_1(\kappa^{(m)}_N)$, with $c^E$ as in [lem-trf-integral-pullback-comparison-realization]. Naturality of $\kappa^{(1)}$ at the isomorphism $
u_{m,C}=a_{m,C}(\kappa^{(m)}_N)^{-1}$ gives $(\kappa^{(1)}_{\mathcal L_sG_mC})^{-1}P_1(
u_{m,C})=F_1(a_{m,C})F_1(\kappa^{(m)}_N)^{-1}(\kappa^{(1)}_{P_mN})^{-1}$. Hence
$$\mathcal L_s(t_{m,C})
u_{1,G_mC}P_1(
u_{m,C})c^E_{m,N}=\mathcal L_s(t_{m,C})a_{1,G_mC}F_1(a_{m,C})d_{m,N}^{-1}(\kappa^{(m+1)}_N)^{-1}=a_{m+1,C}(\kappa^{(m+1)}_N)^{-1}=
u_{m+1,C}.$$
With step 4 this is the stated compositor compatibility. No equality is deduced from individual derived evaluations.

source.place: Ancestor Step 1, Global powers: naturality and compositor compatibility before rationalization

proof.text: For $C=\mathcal R_sN_0$, the reduction construction in [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus] is the strict system $(Q\otimes B_n)_n$ for one flat-term K-flat $Q\to N_0$. If $N_0\in D^b_c(s,R)$, the same completion map of [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison] identifies $\mathcal L_sC$ with $N_0$, naturally and with its actual quotient augmentation. Thus steps 2 and 8 identify the realized power-$r$ map with $\iota_{N_0}^{(r)}$, which recovers the announced reduction-tower case. Conversely a finite-output compact-support system whose derived limit is bounded constructible satisfies exactly the hypothesis used in step 7, regardless of its normalization or Tor-amplitude. Steps 1-6 applied to every system, and steps 7-9 only used derived completeness of that limit. This proves the final scope assertions.
